summary: This informational document describes the cablelabs URN namespace identifier for resources published by Cable Television Laboratories, Inc.

plainLanguage.summary: This reserves a name style so a cable industry lab can give its documents stable names.

questions: what is the cablelabs urn namespace
subtitle: A namespace for identifying cable industry specifications and resources.

tldr.problem: Cable Television Laboratories (CableLabs) develops technical specifications for cable telecommunications including DOCSIS, PacketCable and OpenCable. These specifications need unique, persistent identifiers for data models and resources to ensure systems can reliably reference the same definitions.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 6289 registers the URN Namespace Identifier (NID) 'cablelabs' allowing CableLabs to assign URNs in the format urn:cablelabs:{resource-class}:{resource-specific-string}, managed through CableLabs' Assigned Names and Numbers (CANN) registry.
tldr.outcome: The 'cablelabs' namespace is now an official IANA-registered URN namespace, enabling CableLabs specifications and manufacturers to uniquely identify cable system resources, data models and configurations across all implementations.

today: RFC 6289 registered the 'cablelabs' URN namespace with IANA in 2011. The namespace continues to be used by CableLabs specifications including DOCSIS, PacketCable and OpenCable for device and service identifiers across the cable television industry.

sections.title: CableLabs and the Need for Standard Names
sections.content:
Cable Television Laboratories, Inc. is a non-profit research consortium dedicated to developing cable telecommunications technologies. Its members include product vendors, manufacturers, and cable operator companies. CableLabs organizes work into projects like DOCSIS (Data Over Cable Service Interface Specification), PacketCable for voice services, and OpenCable for set-top boxes, with technical specifications developed collaboratively.

As CableLabs creates data models and specifications, different systems and vendors need to reference the same concepts unambiguously. For example, a cable modem manufacturer needs to know exactly what packet structure a specification refers to, and later versions of that specification need to reference previous versions reliably. URNs provide this stable, persistent naming.

CableLabs decided to register a formal URN namespace with IANA to manage these identifiers centrally rather than allowing each specification to create its own naming scheme.
sections.plainLanguage: CableLabs is a group that makes the technical rules for cable TV systems so that all the different makers' equipment works together. They need official names for all the different parts and settings.

sections.title: The CableLabs URN Structure
sections.content:
The registered namespace identifier is cablelabs. All URNs in this namespace use a two-part structure:

urn:cablelabs:{CLclass}:{CLClassSpecificString}

The CLclass (CableLabs class) identifies a category of resources—such as a specification project, data type, or service definition. Each class has its own naming rules and registration procedures documented in CableLabs standards.

The CLClassSpecificString is the specific identifier within that class. For instance, a hypothetical URN for a user equipment type in the PacketCable Residential SIP Telephony application might be:

urn:cablelabs:packetcable-example:ue:rst-sample

This names both the specification project (PacketCable) and the specific component (user equipment for Residential SIP Telephony).
sections.plainLanguage: Each CableLabs name has a general category—like 'DOCSIS' or 'PacketCable'—and then a specific name within that category. That way different equipment makers know exactly which specification they are implementing.

sections.title: Registry and Community Support
sections.content:
CableLabs maintains the CableLabs' Assigned Names and Numbers (CANN) registry, which documents all registered resource classes and the values assigned within each. This registry is publicly available, ensuring that manufacturers and developers can reference it when implementing CableLabs specifications.

CableLabs specs are licensed to manufacturers on a non-discriminatory basis, and the company provides public access to its registry so that any vendor implementing PacketCable, DOCSIS, or OpenCable equipment can use the same URN identifiers as any other vendor.

The namespace also supports experimental values for testing purposes, though these are not registered permanently. CableLabs may permit sub-registries for certain resource types, allowing secondary entities to manage portions of the namespace under CableLabs oversight.
sections.plainLanguage: CableLabs publishes a list of all the official names so that any company making cable equipment can look them up and use the right names. Everyone gets to see the list and follow the same rules.

sections.title: Why CableLabs Needs Persistent Names
sections.content:
Cable specifications often evolve over time and reference earlier versions. Developers implementing a cable modem or set-top box need to know which versions of which data structures they are supporting. If a specification document says 'implement the configuration structure defined at urn:cablelabs:docsis:config:v3', anyone reading that years later knows exactly which version is meant, even if the specification has been updated.

URNs are location-independent: they identify the resource itself, not a specific file or website. This makes them ideal for long-term technical references that must survive organizational changes, server migrations, and document updates.

The CANN registry works like the IANA number registries that manage IP addresses and port numbers: it is the single source of truth that prevents conflicts and ensures every manufacturer can reliably reference the same specifications.
sections.plainLanguage: If a company building a cable box wants to know 'what does this specification mean?', they look up the official name in the registry and find the right definition. Everyone uses the same names, so equipment from different companies all works together.
